title: Engagement Stability Index (ESI) — playbook and scoring worksheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the Engagement Stability Index (ESI) — a complementary customer health score focused on stability of product engagement over time rather than absolute usage volume. The goal: detect early-stage destabilization (spikes/drops/volatility) that precedes churn and to give CS teams a prioritized, action-oriented view for renewals and adopter success.

Background / why ESI exists (short):
- We already track raw adoption signals (MAU/DAU, seat counts, feature use). Those show 'how much' but not 'how consistent'.
- Customers whose usage is high but highly volatile often renew at lower rates than steady adopters.
- ESI is intended to sit alongside existing health scores (renewal probability, adoption velocity) and provide an orthogonal signal used for escalation and programmatic interventions.

Signal taxonomy (candidate signals we use in ESI):
1) Weekly active seats (WASeats) — rolling 4-week mean and week-to-week delta volatility.
2) Key-route API calls per org (APIroutes) — normalized per-seat, coefficient of variation (CV) over last 8 weeks.
3) Session completion rate for core flows (CoreSR) — % sessions that reach expected end state (e.g., model response + save) measured weekly.
4) Feature adoption breadth (FeatureBreadth) — count of distinct premium features used by 5+ users in org over 12 weeks.
5) Support ticket sentiment (SupSent) — rolling average sentiment score across tickets and their resolution times.
6) Regression alerts hit rate (EvalRegHits) — percentage of eval prompts failing QC thresholds relative to baseline.
7) Admin/Provisioning churn (AdminChurn) — sudden seat removals or API key rotations beyond expected cadence.
8) Executive/Champion touch frequency (ExecTouch) — calendar touches by champion, normalized by contract term.
9) Billing anomalies (BillAnom) — unexpected declines, credits, or invoice disputes.
10) Latency/Errors exposure (PerfErr) — customer-facing error rate and p95 latency anomalies.

Measurement notes (how we make each signal comparable):
- Normalization: every raw signal is converted to a 0-100 scaled metric using a historical baseline per cohort (industry + ARR band). Baselines are calculated as 90-day rolling medians.
- Volatility calculation: for usage signals we use coefficient of variation (std/mean) over a lookback window and then convert CV -> stability score (higher CV -> lower stability).
- Decay: More recent behavior is weighted more heavily. Default half-life: 21 days. Weights across weeks follow exponential decay so a sudden drop last week matters more than 8 weeks ago.
- Seasonality adjustments: for customers with clear periodicity (e.g., weekly batch jobs), seasonality is detected and removed before volatility calc.

Weighting framework (starting draft):
- Engagement stability (usage consistency): 40% -> WASeats (18%), APIroutes (12%), CoreSR (10%)
- Operational risk: 25% -> SupSent (10%), PerfErr (8%), AdminChurn (7%)
- Strategic signals: 20% -> ExecTouch (12%), FeatureBreadth (8%)
- Financial signals: 15% -> BillAnom (10%), EvalRegHits (5%)

Scoring formula (high level):
- For each signal s_i, compute scaled_score_i in 0-100 (higher is better stability).
- ESI_raw = sum_i (w_i * scaled_score_i) / sum_i (w_i)
- Final ESI = round(ESI_raw)
- Map Final ESI to color band: 0-39 Red, 40-64 Amber, 65-100 Green.

Example worksheet (two contrived customer examples):
- Customer A (steady B2B SaaS, 500 seats):
  WASeats score: 78, APIroutes: 84, CoreSR: 72, SupSent: 90, PerfErr: 95, AdminChurn: 88, ExecTouch: 60, FeatureBreadth: 70, BillAnom: 100, EvalRegHits: 95
  Weighted ESI -> ~82 (Green). No immediate play needed; continue standard renew cadence.
- Customer B (fast growth startup, seasonal):
  WASeats score: 55, APIroutes: 42, CoreSR: 60, SupSent: 40, PerfErr: 50, AdminChurn: 30, ExecTouch: 20, FeatureBreadth: 30, BillAnom: 85, EvalRegHits: 40
  Weighted ESI -> ~43 (Amber). Action: schedule product health check, run exploratory log analysis, propose pilot for caching config.

Operational playbook by band:
- Green (>=65):
  - Owner: CSM / automated workflow.
  - Actions: quarterly business review cadence, proactive feature enablement nudges, check-in before renewal window (60d).
  - Escalation: none unless other signals (billing/regression) flash.
- Amber (40-64):
  - Owner: CSM + Solutions Eng (SE) triage within 7 business days.
  - Actions: rapid diagnose runbook: verify seasonality, check recent deploys, run smoke evals, check model variant/quantization change logs. Book 1:1 with champion.
  - Suggested templates: auto email + meeting request + technical checklist (attached below).
- Red (<40):
  - Owner: TL of CS + SE + AM. Must triage within 48 hours.
  - Actions: immediate exec outreach, propose interim mitigations (fallback model variant, dedicated capacity route), prioritize bug fixes or rollback, consider temporary credits for outage. Prepare renewal hold conversation play.

Technical triage checklist (short):
- Verify data freshness for usage metrics (etl lag).
- Compare last 30d metrics vs baseline cohort (ARR + industry).
- Check for recent infra incidents in region (SRE incident IDs).
- Run per-customer eval harness for top 10 prompts used by customer.
- Inspect support tickets for common error strings and tie to release notes.
- Confirm admin actions (seat removals, API key rotations).

Implementation notes and deployment plan (MVP):
1) Prototype ESI in a daily batch job (not real-time) using existing analytics data warehouse; surface score in CS dashboard.
2) Pilot with 30 mid-market customers for 8 weeks, compare ESI-triggered interventions vs control on renewal NPS and retention.
3) Iterate weights using logistic regression / SHAP to predict one-year renewal using ESI and current health score as features.
4) Add ESI to alerting: trigger Amber email to CSM when drop > 20 points in a rolling 14-day window.

Evaluation and tuning guidance:
- Do not overfit weights to ARR band; run stratified holdouts (SMB, mid-market, enterprise).
- Monitor false positives (cases where ESI dropped but no churn within 6 months) and false negatives (steady ESI but churn). Aim to minimize false negatives for enterprise customers.
- Periodically (quarterly) re-run baseline normalization to account for product changes (new features, pricing).

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Half-life: is 21d the right default? Consider A/B test with 14d vs 28d.
- ExecTouch weight: should we weight recent exec touches more heavily than historical? (likely yes).
- Handling of seasonal customers: when seasonality detection fails, fall back to cohort median.
- Response SLA matrix per tier for ESI alerts (CS ops to propose).

Quick action templates (draft snippets):
- Amber email subject: "Quick check-in: recent activity dip — can we sync?" Body: short diagnostic questions + proposed times next 3 days.
- Red outreach: "Urgent: noticed multiple signals affecting your usage — request 30m emergency sync to avoid disruption" + include 3 immediate mitigation options.

Appendix: links and data sources
- Data sources: analytics-warehouse.table.customer_events, billing.transactions, zendesk.tickets, calendar-touch-exports, prod-metrics.perf_errors
- Related artifacts: CONFLUENCE-ESI-12345 (baseline calculations), JIRA CS-7789 (pilot tasks), slack thread customer-health for pilot updates

Next steps (owner: Aisha):
- Finalize decay parameter and implement batch prototype (target: pilot start 2025-02-01).
- Create SE/CS runbook doc and automation templates (emails + playbook checklists).
- Kick off pilot cohort selection with GTM and product.

Notes to self (working):
- Keep this doc intentionally succinct — use linked Confluence for math and tables.
- We will likely need a separate sheet that contains per-customer weekly signal values for triage.
- Add explicit mapping between ESI bands and renewal playbook incentives (credits, dedicated training, SLA uplift).

(End of draft)
